mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 3.0% (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as low interest rates reduce the discount rate for equity valuations and encourage risk-taking.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 3.0% (over a 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate below 4.0% (UNRATE) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as low unemployment indicates a strong labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate profit growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0% (over a 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL value above 255.0 (as of the last month) indicates moderate inflation, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as the Federal Reserve is likely to raise interest rates to combat inflationary pressures.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 255.0 (over a 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 110.0) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as it signals a weakening economy that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 110.0 (over a 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) and strong industrial production (INDPRO > 110.0) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it indicates a robust economy with strong labor market conditions and expanding industrial output, supporting corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0 AND INDPRO > 110.0 (over a 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high unemployment (UNRATE > 4.0%) and declining housing starts (HOUST < 1300.0) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as it indicates a weakening economy with high joblessness and reduced construction activity, leading to lower consumer confidence and spending.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0 AND HOUST < 1300.0 (over a 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 3.0%), high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 255.0) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as the Federal Reserve's rate hikes to combat inflation lead to higher discount rates and reduced equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 3.0% AND CPIAUCSL > 255.0 (over a 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: During a demand expansion (GDPC1 > 19000 and HOUST > 1350.0), positive S&P 500 forward returns are expected over the next 60 trading days, as strong GDP growth and rising housing starts indicate robust consumer and business demand, supporting corporate earnings and equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 > 19000 AND HOUST > 1350.0 (over a 5-year rolling window).
